metadata.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price despite interest from Galatasaray.
metadata.content: Bruno Fernandes transfer news: Manchester United captain not for sale at any price despite Galatasaray interest | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Bruno Fernandes transfer news: Manchester United captain not for sale at any price despite Galatasaray interest Bruno Fernandes broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season last season; Reports have claimed Turkish side Galatasaray are ready to bid for the 31-year-old, who has entered the final year of his contract Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Monday 17 August 2026 16:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all 21 assists from Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes as he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season! Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price despite interest from Galatasaray. Reports have claimed the Turkish side are ready to bid for the 31-year-old, who has entered the final year of his contract, but United also have an option to extend by a further year. However, United will not entertain any offers for their talisman, who was named Premier League Player of the Year last season after breaking the competition's assist record. messages.text: MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year joins Hundred final coverage

metadata.summary: The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday.
metadata.content: Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner for 2026 is Rosa Simkin; the 18-year-old from Warwickshire, who is currently studying yournalism at Cardiff University, joined Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday as part of her prize Monday 17 August 2026 14:28, UK Image: Rosa Simkin interviews Trent Rockets' Georgia Adams for Sky Sports during The Hundred women's final at Lord's (image: Jed Leicester, MCC ) The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday. During the innings break of both the women's and men's finals, Rosa held flash interviews talking to Georgia Adams from Trent Rockets and Noor Ahmad from Manchester Super Giants as both teams ultimately went on to lift the titles. The 18-year-old also presented some of the bitesize highlight videos for Sky Sports Cricket's digital channels and made content for Lord's Instagram, giving audiences an insight into her day as part of the team. metadata.summary: It's been another summer of change at Chelsea - and on the eve of a new Premier League season, there is so much to analyse at the club, with Xabi Alonso's reign kicking off, big-money transfers to be settled and a search for success on the pitch in their sights.
metadata.content: Chelsea podcast: Xabi Alonso, Enzo Fernandez future, transfers and a new era at Stamford Bridge analysed | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Chelsea podcast: Xabi Alonso, Enzo Fernandez future, transfers and a new era at Stamford Bridge analysed Monday 17 August 2026 17:26, UK Image: Listen to the special Sky Sports podcast on Xabi Alonso's Chelsea It's been another summer of change at Chelsea - and on the eve of a new Premier League season, there is so much to analyse at the club, with Xabi Alonso's reign kicking off, big-money transfers to be settled and a search for success on the pitch in their sights. In a special Sky Sports podcast - A big summer for... Chelsea - Peter Smith is joined by Sky Sports News reporter James Savundra and Sky Sports football journalist David Richardson to discuss the key talking points at the club, including Enzo Fernandez's future amid interest from Manchester City and a £120m price tag. The arrival of £117m Morgan Rogers and his partnership with Cole Palmer was also on the agenda, along with Alonso's new tactical set-up and the surprise signings of experienced pair Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, which signalled a shift in the club's transfer policy. messages.text: Rogers on playing with 'artist' Palmer and getting Chelsea back to the top

metadata.summary: Morgan Rogers is convinced Chelsea can once again compete for the top trophies and says he and Cole Palmer know exactly how to play together.
metadata.content: Chelsea's Morgan Rogers relishing prospect of playing with Cole Palmer as he targets Premier League and Champions League glory | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Chelsea's Morgan Rogers relishing prospect of playing with Cole Palmer as he targets Premier League and Champions League glory Morgan Rogers unfazed by price tag and confident of forming effective partnership with Cole Palmer; watch full interview on Premier League Show from 5pm on Sky Sports News; Chelsea visit Fulham in the first Monday Night Football of the season on August 24, kick-off 8pm By Pat Davison and Dev Trehan Monday 17 August 2026 17:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers speaks to Sky Sports after his big-money move to Chelsea and how he plans to play with friend Cole Palmer... Morgan Rogers is convinced Chelsea can once again compete for the top trophies and says he and Cole Palmer know exactly how to play together. Rogers became the most expensive British player of all time when he joined Chelsea from Aston Villa straight after his World Cup exploits where he helped England reach the semi-finals and finish third in the tournament. The 24-year-old scored on his debut in Chelsea's 3-1 win over Real Sociedad on Saturday. "I'm just so excited," Rogers told Sky Sports. "It was just an unbelievable summer. messages.text: How Hunt struck gold with historic Championships display

metadata.summary: Amy Hunt told Sky Sports back in February that three gold medals in Birmingham was the dream. Six months later, she is a four-time European champion and the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships.
metadata.content: Amy Hunt: How British sprinter surpassed her own goal for gold with historic four-medal display at European Championships | Athletics News | Sky Sports Skip to content Amy Hunt: How British sprinter surpassed her own goal for gold with historic four-medal display at European Championships British sprinter Amy Hunt won an incredible four gold medals at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham; Sky Sports examines how the Cambridge-educated athlete came through challenges during the pandemic to secure glory in front of her home fans Ellie Prophet Sports Journalist Monday 17 August 2026 16:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amy Hunt reflects on her record-breaking European Championships, after the Team GB sprinter secured four gold medals. Amy Hunt told Sky Sports back in February that three gold medals in Birmingham was the dream. Six months later, she is a four-time European champion and the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships. Hunt held up four fingers to the camera after winning gold in the mixed 4x100m relay, completing her historic haul. When Sky Sports spoke to the sprinter in February, the World and Olympic silver medallist was looking ahead to Birmingham and the chance to impress on home soil.
